text: Hypothesis 1 — Most likely: Upstream weather-observation feed/ingest service (not enumerated in incident, feeds service:gridcast:forecast-pipeline) :: The upstream feed emitted malformed, missing, or out-of-range weather observations starting around 2026-10-04T20:18:42Z, causing the forecast pipeline's variability.weather_observations check to warn repeatedly until the feed stabilized around 20:30:48Z. :: Input-data degradation most likely triggered the warnings; the forecast pipeline was the affected receiver, not the origin.

Hypothesis 2: service:gridcast:forecast-pipeline :: A recent change or bug in the variability.weather_observations quality-check logic made the threshold or comparison window too strict, flagging normal weather observation variability as a warning repeatedly. :: The fault originates in the forecast pipeline's quality-check code or configuration.

Hypothesis 3: service:gridcast:forecast-pipeline — observation preprocessing/aggregation stage :: A preprocessing or aggregation bug introduced duplicate, stale, or misaligned weather observations into the quality-check input, creating artificial variability spikes. :: The forecast pipeline generated the bad data that its own quality check subsequently flagged.

Hypothesis 4: External weather observation provider/API :: The external provider intermittently returned incomplete station coverage, delayed data, or data gaps during the incident window, causing the forecast pipeline to see higher-than-normal observation variability. :: External dependency degradation produced transient gaps or spikes in weather observations.

Hypothesis 5: Weather-observation data store/cache serving service:gridcast:forecast-pipeline :: The observation store or cache returned inconsistent or stale reads during the incident, causing the forecast pipeline to intermittently see discontinuous observations and emit repeated variability warnings. :: The data-serving layer, not the forecast-pipeline logic, was the source of the bad observations.
